what_it_does:
It supplies stage A's fourth-clause half and the material stage F needs to move or not move W8 A6's mark.

Mapped to W8's parts. A6 says the clause "has not been run" and names two checks: settle the reading, then look in a trainer's record for an occurrence realising a member of H that represents the survival condition. This deliverable runs the second as far as published records reach, and reports exactly where it stops. A5 is served indirectly: A5 is held if A6 holds, so whichever way A6 falls, A5's holder changes, and evidence.md says what each outcome costs A5, B6 and the model's use of the qualified Derivation 3.

Three things it does that the plan did not ask for and the reading forced.

First, the clause names three things and not four. It forbids representation of t, of H, and of the survival condition, and does not forbid representation of mu, the variation operator, although mu is named two sentences earlier in the same definition. A text stating an OPTIMIZER states mu. So the most abundant evidence there is - optimizer papers - falls outside the clause, and I report it separately and keep it out of the W10.3 count. My own task's wording lists the optimizer alongside the loss; the clause does not.

Second, the survival condition is this one, "a survival condition requiring fidelity on H". A generic statement of cross-entropy states a kind of survival condition, not this one. That is why W8 A6 is right that a criterion list is the sharpest candidate: a criterion list is particular to the training it was used on. This narrowing makes the collection harder to satisfy, not easier.

Third, a rival reading neither W8 A6 nor my task names. Part IV says "a selected transport has no represented target and no criticism in its history; a constructed one has both" - so the clause may be what keeps Selected and Constructed apart, in which case it is settled by the declared boundary (are the engineers who wrote the loss inside the system?) and not by corpus membership at all. The change that separates it from the physical reading is written as a poke a judge can run on paper: move the boundary, hold the corpus fixed.

The sharpest test, as a procedure. Three public corpus indices exist over four of the five named corpora - infini-gram (Dolma, RedPajama-1T, Pile, C4, with document search), Data Portraits (Pile, Stack), and "Am I in The Stack". W8 A6 says "Neither check is a run this repository can make", which is true of this repository and not of those indices. The procedure fixes three target documents before searching: row one, PyTorch's cross_entropy definition (the thing the test is meant to catch); row two, the GPT-3 paper (a middle case); row three, the AdamW paper (the nearest innocent neighbour, which states mu and must NOT make the test fire). An examiner who reports row three as settling the clause has shown the test measures presence of machine-learning text, not the clause.

could_not_settle:
Five things, in order of how much they cost.

1. Which reading is right. Nothing collected bears on the strict reading at all; it is settled or not settled inside file 11. I said in predictions.md, before looking, that this outcome would show the collection was the wrong instrument, and for reading (i) it is. The rival reading (iii) may make the corpus evidence beside the point altogether.

2. Representation under (R). Presence of a text stating a loss does not make that text represent the survival condition. (R) needs a faithful transport with selected or constructed provenance, and no corpus record speaks to fidelity or to provenance. This is the link where the case will actually be won or lost, and it is an argument a judge makes, not a search.

3. Membership of any named document. That needs the index run of section 7.3. I did not run it: the plan restricts me to python3 dry runs that send nothing, and an index query is a request to an outside service.

4. Whether the corpus contains a document stating the loss of a model trained on that corpus - the sharpest case my task names. No record documents it. I found no corpus paper saying so, and "I did not find X" describes my search, not the world. The nearest documented approaches are named: the Pile and the AdamW paper (which bears on mu, not the clause); Dolma's code subset and PyTorch (which is what the test targets); Dolma 3 and the OLMo 2 paper (on an unconfirmed date).

5. Whether Claude's constitution is in Claude's corpus. Anthropic publishes cut-offs and no composition. The criterion text was public and public-domain for four months inside Opus 5's window; the record neither says it was in nor says it was out.
for_the_reviewer:
Press here first, in this order.

1. Section 2 of evidence.md, that the clause names three things and not four. Everything downstream is shaped by it: it is why the optimizer evidence is set aside, why the W10.3 count is smaller than it could have been, and why the sharpest test targets a loss and not an optimizer. It was forced by reading, not predicted, and I say so. If a reviewer can show that the survival condition includes the update rule, or that file 10 puts mu in the clause's list, the whole shape of this collection changes and the Pile/AdamW case becomes the finding rather than the foil. I grepped file 11 only.

2. Reading (iii), section 6.3. It is mine, it is not in W8 A6, and if it is right the collection is beside the point. The sentence it rests on - "a selected transport has no represented target and no criticism in its history" - can be read as a gloss on the clause rather than a restatement of it, and I have not closed that. This is the item I would most like a DeepSeek examiner to attack, and the boundary poke is written so it can be run on paper without a key.

3. The Level A / Level B split in section 9. It is the only place where I decided what counts, and my own check half broke it: the Common Pile has a universally quantified sentence too, and is kept out of Level A only by relevance. So the split is two tests wearing one name. A reviewer who thinks the split is a dressed-up ranking should collapse it and see whether the tick survives; I believe it does, at "at least one", but the shape of the report would change.

4. The Anthropic quotations in 5.1. They are the weakest evidence in the file - a search summary of PDFs, not a page read whole - and they carry the sharpest particular candidate in the whole collection. If the reviewer wants that case to bear weight, the system-card PDFs have to be read properly by someone willing to let the tool cache a file.

5. check.py. Run it. It is the only part that can fail on its own, and it caught two faults during the build (the R8 double-count and a miscased quotation of W8 B6).

Two housekeeping facts the reviewer should know. The WebFetch tool wrote one PDF cache file outside my folder, at the session's tool-results directory, when I fetched the Pile datasheet; I did not put it there and I did not delete it, because deleting is also acting outside my folder. After that I avoided PDF fetches. And the owner's Atria Asi instruction (complex analysis, one at a time, larger token ceilings) is A6's and stage E's business, not A3's: no key exists here and nothing was sent anywhere.
